In that case, some treat it as no longer being a complete arbitrage because if the exchange rate moved against the arbitrageur, the profit on the transaction may create a loss.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Interest rate swaps An agreement to swap interest rate exposures from floating to fixed or vice versa. There is no swap of the principal. It is the interest cash flows, be they payments or receipts, that are exchanged.
texts.text: Interest rate swaps An agreement to swap interest rate exposures from floating to fixed or vice versa. There is no swap of the principal. It is the interest cash flows, be they payments or receipts, that are exchanged.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Intermarket spread The sale of a given delivery month of a futures contract on one exchange and the simultaneous purchase of the same delivery month and futures contract on another exchange.
texts.text: Intermarket spread The sale of a given delivery month of a futures contract on one exchange and the simultaneous purchase of the same delivery month and futures contract on another exchange.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Internationalization Referring to a currency that is widely used to denominate trade and credit transactions by nonresidents of the country of issue. The U.S. dollar and the Swiss franc are examples.
texts.text: Internationalization Referring to a currency that is widely used to denominate trade and credit transactions by nonresidents of the country of issue. The U.S. dollar and the Swiss franc are examples.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Intervention Action by a central bank to effect the value of its currency by entering the market. Concerted intervention refers to action by a number of central banks to control exchange rates.
texts.text: Intervention Action by a central bank to effect the value of its currency by entering the market. Concerted intervention refers to action by a number of central banks to control exchange rates.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Introducing broker (IB) A person or an organization that solicits or accepts orders to buy or sell futures contracts or commodity options but does not accept money or other assets from customers to support such orders.
texts.text: Introducing broker (IB) A person or an organization that solicits or accepts orders to buy or sell futures contracts or commodity options but does not accept money or other assets from customers to support such orders.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Inverted market A futures market in which the relationship between two delivery months of the same commodity is abnormal.
texts.text: Inverted market A futures market in which the relationship between two delivery months of the same commodity is abnormal.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Island chart pattern Formed when the market gaps in one direction and then in the next session gaps open in the opposite direction, leaving the prior day's bar or range seeming like an 'island' on the chart. At tops, this is extremely bearish; and at bottoms, it is considered extremely bullish. This is a rare chart pattern and is similar in nature to the Japanese candlestick pattern called the 'abandon baby.'
texts.text: Island chart pattern Formed when the market gaps in one direction and then in the next session gaps open in the opposite direction, leaving the prior day's bar or range seeming like an 'island' on the chart. At tops, this is extremely bearish; and at bottoms, it is considered extremely bullish. This is a rare chart pattern and is similar in nature to the Japanese candlestick pattern called the 'abandon baby.'

texts.label: text
texts.orig: J trader An independent electronic trading order entry platform provider by Pats Systems that routes orders to the exchanges trading systems, such as the Chicago Board of Trade's E-CBOT system and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's GLOBEX system.
texts.text: J trader An independent electronic trading order entry platform provider by Pats Systems that routes orders to the exchanges trading systems, such as the Chicago Board of Trade's E-CBOT system and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's GLOBEX system.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Lagging indicators Market indicators showing the general direction of the economy and confirming or denying the trend implied by the leading indicators.
texts.text: Lagging indicators Market indicators showing the general direction of the economy and confirming or denying the trend implied by the leading indicators.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Last trading day (LTD) The final day on which trading may occur in a given futures or options contract month.
texts.text: Last trading day (LTD) The final day on which trading may occur in a given futures or options contract month.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Leading indicators Market indicators that signal the state of the economy for the coming months. Some of the leading indicators include average manufacturing workweek, initial claims for unemployment insurance, orders for consumer goods and material, percentage of companies reporting slower deliveries, change in manufacturers'  unfilled  orders  for  durable  goods,  plant  and  equipment  orders,  new building permits, index of consumer expectations, change in material prices, prices of stocks, and change in money supply.
texts.text: Leading indicators Market indicators that signal the state of the economy for the coming months. Some of the leading indicators include average manufacturing workweek, initial claims for unemployment insurance, orders for consumer goods and material, percentage of companies reporting slower deliveries, change in manufacturers'  unfilled  orders  for  durable  goods,  plant  and  equipment  orders,  new building permits, index of consumer expectations, change in material prices, prices of stocks, and change in money supply.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: LEAPS Long-Term Equity Anticipation Securities; options that have an extended life as long as five years; generally used for options on stocks.
texts.text: LEAPS Long-Term Equity Anticipation Securities; options that have an extended life as long as five years; generally used for options on stocks.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Leverage The ability to control large dollar amounts of a commodity with a comparatively small amount of capital.
texts.text: Leverage The ability to control large dollar amounts of a commodity with a comparatively small amount of capital.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Liability In terms of foreign exchange, the obligation to deliver to a counterparty an amount of currency either in respect of a balance sheet holding at a specified future date or in respect of an unmatured forward or spot transaction.
texts.text: Liability In terms of foreign exchange, the obligation to deliver to a counterparty an amount of currency either in respect of a balance sheet holding at a specified future date or in respect of an unmatured forward or spot transaction.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Limit order A request to deal as a buyer or a seller for a foreign currency transaction at a specified price or at a better price, if obtainable.
texts.text: Limit order A request to deal as a buyer or a seller for a foreign currency transaction at a specified price or at a better price, if obtainable.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Liquidation Any transaction that offsets or closes out a previously established position.
texts.text: Liquidation Any transaction that offsets or closes out a previously established position.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Liquidity The ability of a market to accept large transactions.
texts.text: Liquidity The ability of a market to accept large transactions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Long The  condition  of  having  bought  futures  contracts  or  owning  a  cash commodity.
texts.text: Long The  condition  of  having  bought  futures  contracts  or  owning  a  cash commodity.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Long-legged doji A specific doji that forms when the open and the close occur near the middle of a wide-range trading session.
texts.text: Long-legged doji A specific doji that forms when the open and the close occur near the middle of a wide-range trading session.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Maintenance margin A set minimum margin that a customer must maintain in his or her margin account. If the cash amount in a trading account drops below the margin level and a margin call is generated, then a trader must either send additional funds to get the account back to the initial margin level or liquidate positions to satisfy the call.
texts.text: Maintenance margin A set minimum margin that a customer must maintain in his or her margin account. If the cash amount in a trading account drops below the margin level and a margin call is generated, then a trader must either send additional funds to get the account back to the initial margin level or liquidate positions to satisfy the call.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Make a market The action of a dealer quoting bid and offer prices at which he or she stands ready to buy and sell.
texts.text: Make a market The action of a dealer quoting bid and offer prices at which he or she stands ready to buy and sell.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Managed float The regular intervention of the monetary authorities in the market to stabilize the rates or to aim the exchange rate in a required direction.
texts.text: Managed float The regular intervention of the monetary authorities in the market to stabilize the rates or to aim the exchange rate in a required direction.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Managed futures Represents an industry comprised of professional money managers known as commodity trading advisors who manage client assets on a discretionary basis, using global futures markets as an investment medium.
texts.text: Managed futures Represents an industry comprised of professional money managers known as commodity trading advisors who manage client assets on a discretionary basis, using global futures markets as an investment medium.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Margin The amount of money or collateral that must be initially provided or thereafter maintained to ensure against losses on open contracts. Initial margin must be placed before a trade is entered. Maintenance or variation margin must be added to initial margin to maintain against losses on open positions. The amount that needs to be present to establish or thereafter maintain is sometimes referred to as 'necessary margin.'
texts.text: Margin The amount of money or collateral that must be initially provided or thereafter maintained to ensure against losses on open contracts. Initial margin must be placed before a trade is entered. Maintenance or variation margin must be added to initial margin to maintain against losses on open positions. The amount that needs to be present to establish or thereafter maintain is sometimes referred to as 'necessary margin.'

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Margin call A claim by one's broker or dealer for additional good faith performance monies, usually issued when an investor's account suffers adverse price movements.
texts.text: Margin call A claim by one's broker or dealer for additional good faith performance monies, usually issued when an investor's account suffers adverse price movements.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Market maker A person or firm authorized to create and maintain a market in an instrument.
texts.text: Market maker A person or firm authorized to create and maintain a market in an instrument.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Market order An order to buy or to sell a financial instrument immediately at the best possible price.
texts.text: Market order An order to buy or to sell a financial instrument immediately at the best possible price.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Market profile A method of charting that analyzes price and volume in specific time brackets.
texts.text: Market profile A method of charting that analyzes price and volume in specific time brackets.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Mark to market The daily adjustment of an account to reflect accrued profits and losses; often required to calculate variations of margins.
texts.text: Mark to market The daily adjustment of an account to reflect accrued profits and losses; often required to calculate variations of margins.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Microeconomics The study of economic activity as it applies to individual firms or well-defined small groups of individuals or economic sectors.
texts.text: Microeconomics The study of economic activity as it applies to individual firms or well-defined small groups of individuals or economic sectors.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Midprice or middle rate The price halfway between two prices, or the average of both buying and selling prices offered by the market makers.
texts.text: Midprice or middle rate The price halfway between two prices, or the average of both buying and selling prices offered by the market makers.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Minimum price fluctuation The smallest increment of market price movement possible in a given futures contract.
texts.text: Minimum price fluctuation The smallest increment of market price movement possible in a given futures contract.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Momentum The measure of the rate of change in prices.
texts.text: Momentum The measure of the rate of change in prices.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Morning doji star A bullish three-candle formation in which the middle candle is formed by a doji.
texts.text: Morning doji star A bullish three-candle formation in which the middle candle is formed by a doji.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Moving average A way of smoothing a set of data; widely used in price time series.
texts.text: Moving average A way of smoothing a set of data; widely used in price time series.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: National Futures Association (NFA) The self-regulatory agency for futures and options markets. The primary responsibilities of the NFA are to enforce ethical standards and customer protection rules, to screen futures professionals for membership, to audit and monitor professionals for financial and general compliance rules, and to provide for arbitration of futures-related disputes.
texts.text: National Futures Association (NFA) The self-regulatory agency for futures and options markets. The primary responsibilities of the NFA are to enforce ethical standards and customer protection rules, to screen futures professionals for membership, to audit and monitor professionals for financial and general compliance rules, and to provide for arbitration of futures-related disputes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Nearby month The futures contract month closest to expiration. Also called the spot month .
texts.text: Nearby month The futures contract month closest to expiration. Also called the spot month .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Net position The amount of currency bought or sold that has not yet been offset by opposite transactions.
texts.text: Net position The amount of currency bought or sold that has not yet been offset by opposite transactions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Offer The price at which a seller is willing to sell; the best offer is the lowest such price available.
texts.text: Offer The price at which a seller is willing to sell; the best offer is the lowest such price available.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Offset The closing out or liquidation of a futures position.
texts.text: Offset The closing out or liquidation of a futures position.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Offshore The operations of a financial institution that, although physically located in a country, has little connection with that country's financial systems. In certain countries, a bank is not permitted to do business in the domestic market but only with other foreign banks; this is known as an 'offshore banking unit.'
texts.text: Offshore The operations of a financial institution that, although physically located in a country, has little connection with that country's financial systems. In certain countries, a bank is not permitted to do business in the domestic market but only with other foreign banks; this is known as an 'offshore banking unit.'

texts.label: text
texts.orig: One cancels other A contingency order instructing a broker to cancel one side of a two-sided entry order.
texts.text: One cancels other A contingency order instructing a broker to cancel one side of a two-sided entry order.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Opening range A range of prices at which buy and sell transactions take place during the first minute of the opening of the market for most markets.
texts.text: Opening range A range of prices at which buy and sell transactions take place during the first minute of the opening of the market for most markets.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Open interest The total number of futures or options contracts of a given commodity that have been neither offset by an opposite futures or option transaction nor fulfilled by delivery of the commodity or option exercise. Each open transaction has a buyer and a seller; but for calculation of open interest, only one side of the contract is counted.
texts.text: Open interest The total number of futures or options contracts of a given commodity that have been neither offset by an opposite futures or option transaction nor fulfilled by delivery of the commodity or option exercise. Each open transaction has a buyer and a seller; but for calculation of open interest, only one side of the contract is counted.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Open outcry Method of public auction for making verbal bids and offers in the trading pits or rings of futures exchanges.
texts.text: Open outcry Method of public auction for making verbal bids and offers in the trading pits or rings of futures exchanges.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Option A contract that conveys the right, but not the obligation, to buy or to sell a particular item at a certain price for a limited time.
texts.text: Option A contract that conveys the right, but not the obligation, to buy or to sell a particular item at a certain price for a limited time.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Out-of-the-money option An option with no intrinsic value; i.e., a call whose strike price is above the current futures price or a put whose strike price is below the current futures price.
texts.text: Out-of-the-money option An option with no intrinsic value; i.e., a call whose strike price is above the current futures price or a put whose strike price is below the current futures price.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Overbought The condition of a specific move when the market price has risen too far too fast and is set up for a corrective pullback or period of consolidation; the opposite of oversold .
texts.text: Overbought The condition of a specific move when the market price has risen too far too fast and is set up for a corrective pullback or period of consolidation; the opposite of oversold .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Overnight A deal from today until the next business day.
texts.text: Overnight A deal from today until the next business day.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Overnight limit Net long or short position in one or more currencies that a dealer can carry over into the next dealing day. Passing the book to other bank dealing rooms in the next trading time zone reduces the need for dealers to maintain these unmonitored exposures.
texts.text: Overnight limit Net long or short position in one or more currencies that a dealer can carry over into the next dealing day. Passing the book to other bank dealing rooms in the next trading time zone reduces the need for dealers to maintain these unmonitored exposures.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Oversold The condition of a specific move when the market price has fallen and is in a position for a corrective rally or a period of consolidation; the opposite of overbought .
texts.text: Oversold The condition of a specific move when the market price has fallen and is in a position for a corrective rally or a period of consolidation; the opposite of overbought .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Par The face value of a security; e.g., a bond selling at par is worth the same dollar amount it was issued for or at which it will be redeemed at maturity.
texts.text: Par The face value of a security; e.g., a bond selling at par is worth the same dollar amount it was issued for or at which it will be redeemed at maturity.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Parities The value of one currency in terms of another.
texts.text: Parities The value of one currency in terms of another.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pegged A system where a currency moves in line with another currency; some pegs are strict while others have bands of movement.
texts.text: Pegged A system where a currency moves in line with another currency; some pegs are strict while others have bands of movement.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Piercing pattern A candlestick formation involving two candles formed at bottoms of market moves. The first candle is a long dark candle; the second candle opens lower than the dark candle's low and closes more than half way above the first candle's real body.
texts.text: Piercing pattern A candlestick formation involving two candles formed at bottoms of market moves. The first candle is a long dark candle; the second candle opens lower than the dark candle's low and closes more than half way above the first candle's real body.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: PIP (percentage in points) One unit of price change in the bid/ask price of a currency. For most currencies, it denotes the fourth decimal place in an exchange rate and represents 1/100 of 1 percent (0.01%).
texts.text: PIP (percentage in points) One unit of price change in the bid/ask price of a currency. For most currencies, it denotes the fourth decimal place in an exchange rate and represents 1/100 of 1 percent (0.01%).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pit The area on the trading floor where futures and options on futures contracts are bought and sold. It is customary for Chicago markets to refer to the individual commodity trading areas as pits, whereas in New York, they are referred to as 'rings.'
texts.text: Pit The area on the trading floor where futures and options on futures contracts are bought and sold. It is customary for Chicago markets to refer to the individual commodity trading areas as pits, whereas in New York, they are referred to as 'rings.'

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pivot points The mathematical calculation formula used to determine the support or resistance ranges in a given time period. These formulas can be used to calculate intraday, daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly ranges.
texts.text: Pivot points The mathematical calculation formula used to determine the support or resistance ranges in a given time period. These formulas can be used to calculate intraday, daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly ranges.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Point-and-figure A charting style that tracks the market's price action by representing increases with plotting Xs on a chart and downside corrections with Os. Time is not an issue with this method; rather, it is concerned with pure price movement.
texts.text: Point-and-figure A charting style that tracks the market's price action by representing increases with plotting Xs on a chart and downside corrections with Os. Time is not an issue with this method; rather, it is concerned with pure price movement.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Position The netted total commitments in a given currency; can be flat or square (no exposure), long (more currency bought than sold), or short ( more currency sold than bought).
texts.text: Position The netted total commitments in a given currency; can be flat or square (no exposure), long (more currency bought than sold), or short ( more currency sold than bought).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Premium The dollar value amount placed on an option.
texts.text: Premium The dollar value amount placed on an option.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Prime rate Interest rate charged by major banks to their most creditworthy customers.
texts.text: Prime rate Interest rate charged by major banks to their most creditworthy customers.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Producer Price Index An index that shows the cost of goods and services to producers and wholesalers.
texts.text: Producer Price Index An index that shows the cost of goods and services to producers and wholesalers.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Profit taking The unwinding of a position to realize profits.
texts.text: Profit taking The unwinding of a position to realize profits.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Put option An option that gives the option buyer the right but not the obligation to sell an underlying futures contract at the strike price on or before the expiration date.
texts.text: Put option An option that gives the option buyer the right but not the obligation to sell an underlying futures contract at the strike price on or before the expiration date.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Quote An indicative price; the price quoted for information purposes but not to deal.
texts.text: Quote An indicative price; the price quoted for information purposes but not to deal.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rally A recovery in price after a period of decline.
texts.text: Rally A recovery in price after a period of decline.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Range The  difference  between  the  highest  and  the  lowest  prices  of  a  future recorded during a given trading session.
texts.text: Range The  difference  between  the  highest  and  the  lowest  prices  of  a  future recorded during a given trading session.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rate (1) The price of one currency in terms of another, normally against the U.S. dollar (USD); (2) assessment of the creditworthiness of an institution.
texts.text: Rate (1) The price of one currency in terms of another, normally against the U.S. dollar (USD); (2) assessment of the creditworthiness of an institution.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Reaction A decline in prices following an advance.
texts.text: Reaction A decline in prices following an advance.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Real body The section of a candlestick defined as the area established between the opening and the closing of a particular time period.
texts.text: Real body The section of a candlestick defined as the area established between the opening and the closing of a particular time period.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Reciprocal currency A currency that is normally quoted as dollars per unit of currency rather than as the normal quote of units of currency per dollar. Sterling is the most common example.
texts.text: Reciprocal currency A currency that is normally quoted as dollars per unit of currency rather than as the normal quote of units of currency per dollar. Sterling is the most common example.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Relative Strength Index A technical indicator used to determine a market in an overbought or oversold condition; was developed by Welles Wilder Jr. to help determine market reversals.
texts.text: Relative Strength Index A technical indicator used to determine a market in an overbought or oversold condition; was developed by Welles Wilder Jr. to help determine market reversals.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Resistance point or level A price recognized by technical analysts as a price that is likely to result in a rebound but if broken through is likely to result in a significant price movement.
texts.text: Resistance point or level A price recognized by technical analysts as a price that is likely to result in a rebound but if broken through is likely to result in a significant price movement.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Revaluation Increase in the exchange rate of a currency as a result of official action.
texts.text: Revaluation Increase in the exchange rate of a currency as a result of official action.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Revaluation rate The rate for any period or currency that is used to revalue a position or book.
texts.text: Revaluation rate The rate for any period or currency that is used to revalue a position or book.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rickshaw doji A doji that has an unusually large trading range.
texts.text: Rickshaw doji A doji that has an unusually large trading range.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Risk management The identification and acceptance or offsetting of the risks threatening the profitability or existence of an organization; with respect to foreign exchange, involves consideration of market, sovereign, country, transfer, delivery, credit, and counterparty risk, among other things.
texts.text: Risk management The identification and acceptance or offsetting of the risks threatening the profitability or existence of an organization; with respect to foreign exchange, involves consideration of market, sovereign, country, transfer, delivery, credit, and counterparty risk, among other things.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Risk position An asset or liability that is exposed to fluctuations in value through changes in exchange rates or interest rates.
texts.text: Risk position An asset or liability that is exposed to fluctuations in value through changes in exchange rates or interest rates.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rollover An overnight swap; specifically, the next business day against the following business day; also called 'tomorrow next' (Tom-next).
texts.text: Rollover An overnight swap; specifically, the next business day against the following business day; also called 'tomorrow next' (Tom-next).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Round trip Buying and selling of a specified amount of currency.
texts.text: Round trip Buying and selling of a specified amount of currency.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Same-day transaction A transaction that matures on the day the transaction takes place.
texts.text: Same-day transaction A transaction that matures on the day the transaction takes place.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Scalper A trader who trades for small, short-term profits.
texts.text: Scalper A trader who trades for small, short-term profits.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Selling rate Rate at which a bank is willing to sell foreign currency.
texts.text: Selling rate Rate at which a bank is willing to sell foreign currency.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Settlement date The date on which foreign exchange contracts settle.
texts.text: Settlement date The date on which foreign exchange contracts settle.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Settlement price The last price paid for a commodity on any trading day. The exchange clearinghouse determines a firm's net gains or losses, margin requirements, and the next day's price limits, based on each futures and options contract settlement price; also referred to as 'daily settlement price' or 'daily closing price.'
texts.text: Settlement price The last price paid for a commodity on any trading day. The exchange clearinghouse determines a firm's net gains or losses, margin requirements, and the next day's price limits, based on each futures and options contract settlement price; also referred to as 'daily settlement price' or 'daily closing price.'

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Shadow The area on a candlestick between the high or the low in relation to the open or the close.
texts.text: Shadow The area on a candlestick between the high or the low in relation to the open or the close.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Shooting  star The candle that forms at tops of markets where the shadow is at least twice the length of the real body and the real body forms near the low for the session with little or no shadow at the bottom. This candle resembles an inverted hammer.
texts.text: Shooting  star The candle that forms at tops of markets where the shadow is at least twice the length of the real body and the real body forms near the low for the session with little or no shadow at the bottom. This candle resembles an inverted hammer.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Short The position in a futures market where a trader sells a contract with the intention of buying it back at a lower price for a profit or if at a higher price for a loss. An option trader would be considered 'short the option' if he or she were a writer of that option.
texts.text: Short The position in a futures market where a trader sells a contract with the intention of buying it back at a lower price for a profit or if at a higher price for a loss. An option trader would be considered 'short the option' if he or she were a writer of that option.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Short sale The sale of a specified amount of currency not owned by the seller at the time of the trade; usually made in expectation of a decline in the price.
texts.text: Short sale The sale of a specified amount of currency not owned by the seller at the time of the trade; usually made in expectation of a decline in the price.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Slippage Refers to the negative (or depreciating) price value between where a stop-loss order becomes a market order and where that market order may be filled.
texts.text: Slippage Refers to the negative (or depreciating) price value between where a stop-loss order becomes a market order and where that market order may be filled.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Speculator An investor who is looking to profit from buying or selling derivative products with the anticipation of profiting from price moves by trading in and out of their positions.
texts.text: Speculator An investor who is looking to profit from buying or selling derivative products with the anticipation of profiting from price moves by trading in and out of their positions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Spinning tops A candle where the real body is small in nature with a large range and with shadows at both ends.
texts.text: Spinning tops A candle where the real body is small in nature with a large range and with shadows at both ends.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Spot price The price at which a currency is currently trading in the spot market.
texts.text: Spot price The price at which a currency is currently trading in the spot market.

texts.orig: Swap The simultaneous purchase and sale of the same amount of a given currency for two different dates against the sale and the purchase of another. A swap can be a swap against a forward. In essence, swapping is somewhat similar to borrowing one currency and lending another for the same period. However, any rate of return or cost of funds is expressed in the price differential between the two sides of the transaction.
